pluginRegisterTitle: Allow plugin into the Sigil allow-list
pluginSha256Prose: Keeper computed the hash itself from the host's local cache. Integrity authority is sha256 + Keeper's signature (not the git tag ref).
pluginSigilDisabledBody: The plugin allow-list (Sigil) is not active in this cluster. Sigil is enabled on the Keeper side — ask the Keeper administrator to enable SigilSvc in the configuration.
provPolicyAntiLockout: The list cannot be empty — this would block creation of new operators.
provPolicyDefaultHint: No policy set — all methods are allowed (default behaviour).
provPolicyDesc: Controls which methods can be used to create new operators (Archons). Does not affect login for existing operators.
rbacAssignAllRoles: The operator is already a member of all cluster roles.
rbacAssignProse: The operator will get all permissions of the selected role. The operation is idempotent.
rbacAwaitingParent: Pick the role to derive from above — the narrowing and the permission set are read against its ceiling.
rbacCeilingPanelPermsEmpty: {{name}} grants nothing — a role derived from it would be empty.
rbacCeilingPanelProse: Everything below comes from {{name}} as the server resolved it. Pick a subset of these permissions and narrow the scope; anything beyond is refused with 403.
rbacCeilingPanelScopeUnrestricted: unrestricted — the parent imposes no scope
rbacChildrenProse: They inherit this role's scope, so a change here travels: narrowing it narrows them, WIDENING it widens them. Revoking a permission leaves their row in place but stops granting it.
rbacDeleteBuiltinWarn: This is a builtin role — the server will return 409 role-builtin. Deletion is forbidden.
rbacDeleteNoOperators: The role has no operators — deletion affects only the record itself.
rbacDeleteWarn: Role permissions and membership are cascade-deleted. The action is irreversible.
rbacEditBuiltinWarn: This is a builtin role — the server will return 409 role-builtin. Editing is disabled.
rbacEditReplaceProse: Replace semantics: the checked set fully replaces the existing one. Tick the permissions you need in the catalog below.
rbacEffectiveCountTitle: stored rows → what the role actually grants once the parent is applied
rbacErrParentRequired: Pick the role to derive from. Every role is carved out of another role, so this cannot be empty.
rbacErrPermissionsInvalid: One or more permissions are invalid — check scope values (no spaces).
rbacFullAccessCatalogDimmed: Full access covers every resource — the selections below are redundant.
rbacFullAccessHint: Full access = cluster-admin. Add conditions to bound it to a group (scoped admin).
rbacNoResourceMatch: No resources match — adjust the search, or select one on the left.
rbacParentCatalogUnavailable: The role catalog is unavailable, so there is nothing to derive from — a role cannot be created here right now.
rbacParentDerivedHint: Derived role — inherits from {{name}} and can never exceed it. Changing the scope of {{name}} later changes this role too.
rbacParentNoneHeld: You hold no roles to derive from. Ask for the role you need first.
rbacParentRequiredHint: Pick the role this one is carved out of. It becomes the ceiling: the new role can never exceed it.
rbacParentUnresolved: This role derives from {{name}}, which is not in the catalog you can read — the inherited ceiling is not shown, but the server still enforces it.
rbacPermBeyondCaller: Outside your own rights — you cannot grant what you don't hold.
rbacPermBeyondParent: Outside {{name}} — a derived role cannot exceed its parent.
rbacPermCatalogEmpty: Permission catalog is unavailable. The role's existing permissions are kept on save.
rbacPermPreserved: Permissions outside the catalog (kept as is):
rbacPermSubsetOfCaller: Only what you hold yourself: the rest of the catalog is disabled — the server would refuse it.
rbacPermSubsetOfParent: Subset of {{name}} only: everything it does not grant is disabled below.
rbacPermissionsHint: May be left empty — add later via Role permissions.
rbacRoleScopeCallerFloor: You hold the picked permissions only under {{scope}}. A plain role with no scope would grant them everywhere — wider than you hold them — and the server refuses that. Set a scope inside {{scope}}, or derive from a role instead so the scope stays linked.
rbacRoleScopeDeltaProse: Only the narrowing you add on top of {{name}}. The scope of {{name}} is conjoined by the server — do not restate it here.
rbacRoleScopeProse: Applies to every permission of the role that carries no scope of its own. Leave it unrestricted to keep the permissions as they are.
rbacScopeCeilingCapped: Your rights (inherited) — new grants are capped to this:
rbacScopeCeilingParentCapped: {{name}} already narrows this — you can only narrow further than:
rbacScopeCeilingParentUnrestricted: {{name}} restricts nothing here — your conditions below are the whole rule.
rbacScopeCeilingUnrestricted: Your ceiling: unrestricted — you can grant any scope.
rbacScopeDeltaLegend: Dashed = inherited from {{name}} (read-only). Solid = your own narrowing, the only part this role stores.
rbacScopeDeltaNoneYet: No narrowing of your own yet — the role gets exactly the scope of {{name}}.
rbacScopeDeltaUnrestrictedHint: The role inherits the scope of {{name}} as is. Switch to "By conditions" to narrow it further — you can never widen it.
rbacScopeEmpty: No conditions yet — add one above.
rbacScopeModePinProse: Stores {{scope}} together with your narrowing, so a later widening of {{name}} cannot reach this role. A later narrowing still does. Note that the pinned predicate then stays until someone edits this role.
rbacScopeModeTrackProse: Stores only your narrowing. The role follows {{name}} both ways — if {{name}} is narrowed later this role narrows too, and if it is WIDENED this role widens with it.
rbacScopeRawParseFail: This scope couldn't be parsed into the builder. Edit the raw expression below.
rbacScopeUnrestrictedHint: The permission applies everywhere. Switch to "By conditions" to narrow it.
rbacWildcardActiveProse: Grants every action of {{resource}}, including actions added in future updates. Individual actions are hidden — they're all covered.
